tasks.short: Investigate soil and water quality problems

steps.what: Investigate soil problems and poor water quality through site evidence and competing source hypotheses

tasks.design: Retain site investigation and source assessment with the scientist, recording evidence in {DOCS}. Existing maps and laboratory records inform hypotheses, while causal interpretation requires local investigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources and effects depend on hydrology, management history and incomplete sampling.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records help compare explanations without resolving them automatically.
tasks.still_hard: A spatial association may reflect transport or sampling bias rather than the source.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist chooses discriminating observations and states alternative explanations.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in field investigation or causal reasoning.

reach.learn: Link soil observations to water movement and exposure context.

evidence.claim: Copernicus Land Monitoring Service provides land cover, land use and water data; those data do not establish local pollution sources.

assumptions: Boundary is source-and-effects investigation; routine laboratory execution and remediation implementation are separately scoped.
Scientist assesses site evidence and findings within s1; no preclassified pollution source or degradation flag is assumed.
Consider existing native mapping and records first. Zero upkeep because no new automated workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which additional observation would distinguish a local source from transported contamination?

already_counted.description: All site investigation and causal interpretation remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. No field investigation or source attribution work is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate soil responses to management practices

steps.what: Investigate soils under management practices and check the experimental comparison dataset
Calculate specified soil productivity comparisons and produce repeatable diagnostic plots
Interpret soils responses, test analytical assumptions and assess use capabilities and practice effects

tasks.design: Configure a checked {SPREADSHEET} analysis workbook to repeat explicitly chosen comparisons and diagnostic plots. The scientist retains field investigation, dataset reconciliation, analytical choices and interpretation in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated arithmetic and plotting followed the same already chosen comparison plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas and chart templates can replay those operations with versioned inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Weather, spatial dependence and treatment selection can confound apparent practice effects.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist judges comparability and avoids causal claims unsupported by study design.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated calculation; scientific interpretation remains unchanged.

reach.learn: Explain limits on transferring experimental findings to a different field.

evidence.claim: Repeatable soil response calculations from checked data are model knowledge; no digest case measures this task's labour savings.

assumptions: Boundary includes field investigation and analysis of management responses; experiment setup for unrelated plant mechanisms and advisory implementation are separate.

In s1 scientist produces plot IDs, treatments, dates, soil measurements, units, productivity outcomes, replicate/block IDs, missingness reasons, exclusions and chosen comparison formulas. Capture, reconciliation and analytical specification are counted; ambiguous records or unsuitable assumptions require manual analysis.
Try native workbook configuration first. Existing automatic statistics runtime is not human effort and earns no new saving.
research_questions: Do repeated analyses preserve block structure and expose spatial or missing-data bias?

already_counted.description: Field evidence preparation and contextual scientific interpretation.

incremental.description: Maintain checked formulas and reference datasets.
Research data steward maintains dataset version access.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gross=20 net=13 after 7 upkeep. Zero if analysis is already scripted; 3 if a limited recurring comparison and plot set benefits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct experiments on plant growth and environmental response while observing mechanisms and unexpected effects

tasks.design: Keep experimental execution and mechanism investigation with the scientist, recording evidence in {DOCS}. Existing growth and measurement equipment supports experiments, while biological variation and causal interpretation remain scientific work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Living systems and changing environmental conditions require observation and adaptive investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment supports controlled experiments without eliminating their physical execution.
tasks.still_hard: Observed growth differences may have several interacting causes.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist recognises unexpected responses and chooses follow-up experiments.
tasks.altitude: No assumed reduction in physical experiments or mechanism reasoning.

reach.learn: Choose measurements that distinguish plausible physiological explanations.

evidence.claim: Physical plant experiments and mechanism interpretation remain human scientific work, based on model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is plant mechanism experiment execution and interpretation; soil management comparisons and separate reporting are excluded.
Scientist produces observations and checks environmental conditions during s1; no free structured biological-response or mechanism flag is assumed.
Consider existing native equipment configuration first; unattended growth time is not human labour. Zero upkeep because no new workflow is introduced.
research_questions: Which follow-up experiment separates the leading explanations for the observed growth response?

already_counted.description: All experiment execution and scientific interpretation remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Physical experiments remain unchanged; unattended biological time creates no labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify degraded soils and plan improvement

steps.what: Identify degraded or contaminated soils and develop context-specific plans to improve soil characteristics

tasks.design: Retain soil condition assessment and improvement planning with the scientist, recording the rationale in {DOCS}. Existing evidence and maps inform options, while intervention suitability depends on local conditions and intended land use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Improvement options involve interacting chemical, physical and biological constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing evidence access helps planning without establishing a reliable automatic remediation plan.
tasks.still_hard: An intervention can mobilise contamination or improve one property while worsening another.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist recognises site-specific tradeoffs and identifies specialist assessment needs.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in assessment or planning authority.

reach.learn: Translate scientific constraints into monitored practical actions.

evidence.claim: Site-specific soil improvement planning remains human judgement, based on model knowledge; no applicable digest automation result is established.

assumptions: Boundary is condition identification and intervention planning; source investigation already counted elsewhere and physical remediation implementation are excluded.
Scientist evaluates raw findings and produces condition judgements during s1; no structured suitability, contamination class or improvement target is supplied for free.
Consider native evidence and mapping tools first. Zero upkeep because no new model or capture workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Site constraints and intended land use
research_questions: What monitoring evidence would show that an intervention worsens another soil property?

already_counted.description: All soil assessment and intervention planning remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Scientific assessment and site-specific improvement planning remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated soil response calculations can shrink while field investigation, experiments and intervention planning remain scientific work.
reach: Connect soil evidence to agronomic practice, hydrological pathways and land management constraints.
role.ambitious_version: A scientist whose repeated comparisons are reproducible and whose field recommendations remain grounded in local evidence.
